results.summary: This design is a voltage-controlled ring oscillator whose frequency can be set either by the analog VCTRL pin or by an 8-bit DAC when VCTRL is left open. The DAC_enable pin must be held high for DAC control, and the oscillator output is also provided divided by 64 on OSC_OUT_DIV. Testing involves varying VCTRL or the DAC bits and measuring the output frequency with an oscilloscope. External hardware needed is a power supply for VCTRL and an oscilloscope.

results.summary: This design divides the 10 MHz input clock with a 24-bit compare register to produce a counter that increments once per second by default. The eight inputs program bits 11 to 18 of the compare register, so non-zero inputs change the counting rate. The low eight bits of the counter are driven onto the bidirectional pins, and combinational logic converts the count to decimal for a seven-segment display. After reset the counter should advance once per second with a 10 MHz clock, and the inputs can be changed to experiment with the speed.

results.summary: This project tests prototype SKY130 ROM macros modified to remove the LVT implant on the bitcell. Registers in front of the ROM macros let the user load an address and capture data at controlled intervals using the various clock pins. Meaningful timing testing requires FPGA hardware to drive the control signals with precise timing, and the exact platform is still to be determined. Silicon test reports say it works, with all ROM read successfully at 10 ns propagation time, though more precise hardware would be needed for full timing characterisation.
